Title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Extend Topstitch
Content: Objective When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. When using the Free Topstitch tool, the starting point is going to be the first click point. Location Topstitch Property Editor Extend Start / Extend End Operation Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Extend Start / Extend End
ContentDescription: This web page provides a concise guide on how to adjust the start and end points of a Topstitch to align with the Pattern outline using the Topstitch Property Editor.

Title: Delete Topstitch
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Topstitches. Location Pop-up Menu (Right-click On Topstitch) Delete Operation Click Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pop-up Menu (Right-click On Topstitch) Delete
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for deleting unnecessary topstitches using the pop-up menu and the Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D toolbar.

Title: Free Topstitch
Content: Objective Create a Topstitch to freely sew regardless of the points of Pattern or Internal Shape. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar Free Topstitch Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Free Topstitch 2D Toolbar Free Topstitch Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. The selected area appears in red color. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. The tTopstitch is now created with being highlighted. Note: Click-and-drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0). Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length (ver4.2.0).
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to guide users in creating customizable Topstitches effortlessly using the 2D Toolbar, allowing for precise sewing regardless of the pattern or internal shape.

Title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Exaggerate Topstitch
Content: Objective Express the caved line when topstitches are stitched on the real garment. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor 3D Operation Follow the indicated guieline: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor 3D Toggle on the 3D option. 3D shadow is added under the Topstitch to express the caved line. Use below options to adjust the caved line's Intensity or Thickness. Option Description Normal Map Select the Normal Map. Intensity (%) Adjust the caved line's intensity. Thickness Adjust the caved line's thickness.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a guide for expressing and adjusting the caved line effect of topstitches on garments using 3D settings in the Property Editor.

Title: Show/Hide Topstitch (Below ver.10)
Content: Objective Show or hide Topstitches as needed. Location Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Topstitches 2D Toolbar Show 2D Topstitches Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Topstitches 2D Toolbar Show 2D Topstitches All Topstitches in the 2D window will now be displayed or hidden.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to easily show or hide Topstitches in the 2D window through the Main Menu and 2D Toolbar options.

Title: Edit Topstitch
Content: Objective Relocate or adjust length of Topstitches. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Operation Relocate Topstitch Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Click on a topstitch to change its location. The selected Topstitch is being highlighted. Drag to a desired location. Adjust Topstitch Length Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Click and drag one of the two end points of a Topstitch to adjust its length. The selected Topstitch is now being adjusted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidelines for relocating and adjusting the length of Topstitches using the 2D Toolbar and Main Menu features.

Title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Open/Save Topstitch Item
Content: Objective Save frequently used Topstitch styles in *.sst file format and open to use them in other projects. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor Save Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor Save The selected Topstitch item is saved in .sst file format. To open the saved Topstitch file, click the Open button next to Save.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for saving and opening frequently used Topstitch styles in *.sst file format for use in various projects.

Title: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Edit Topstitch using the right-click pop-up menu. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Right click on the Topstitch to be edited. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Refer to below table and choose appropriate option in need. Option Name Select All With Same Property All Topstitches that have the same properties with the selected one are selected. Assign to New Topstitch A new Topstitch style is applied to the selected Topstitch. A new Topstitch style is created in the Object Browser when this option is selected. Delete Delete the selected Topstitch. Add Internal Line on Topstitch (ver4.2.0) Create an Internal Shape right on top of the selected Topstitch.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on editing Topstitches using the right-click pop-up menu in the 2D Toolbar, detailing options for selection, assignment, deletion, and the addition of internal lines.

Title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Topstitch Corner Type
Content: Objective Set Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. Note: If stitch type is Overlock, set the corner type to Curved for smoother extension. Location Topstitch Property Editor Curved/Right Angled On / Off Operation Curved Corner Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Curved On The selected Topstitch is now being curved and smoothly extended. Right Angled Corner Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Right Angled On The selected topstitch is now being curved at a right angle.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the corner type of topstitches in the Topstitch Property Editor for smoother stitching at corners.

Title: Segment Topstitch
Content: Objective Create a Segment Topstitch (Patterns or Internal Shapes that are split by points). Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Segment Topstitch 2D Toolbar Segment Topstitch Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Segment Topstitch 2D Toolbar Segment Topstitch Click on a segment to create a Topstitch. The Segment Topstitch is created on the selected segment with being highlighted. Note: Click-and-drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0).
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create and apply Segment Topstitches using the 2D Toolbar and Main Menu in your design software.

Title: Reset Topstitch Style Property
Content: Objective Reset Topstitch style properties to default values (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Right-Click Topstitch Style Pop-Up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Right-Click Topstitch Style Pop-Up Menu Reset The Topstitch style properties are now being reset back to default value.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for resetting Topstitch style properties to their default values in version 2.5.0 using the Object Browser's Topstitch Tab.

Title: Create Additional Topstitch Style
Content: Objective Create a new Topstitch style. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab +Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab +Add A new item named Topstitch_1 is now being added with the same property of Default_Topstitch. Note: Additional items are added with names of Topstitch_1,2,3. If there are multiple Topstitch styles in the Topstitch tab when creating a Topstitch on a Pattern, click on the desired Topstitch style and create. To create an additional Topstitch style with existing *.sst file, navigate to the Library Hardware and Trims Topstitch and drag and drop the desired Topstitch style to the Topstitch tab. Or, find the Topstitch file in the File Broswer window and drag and drop.
ContentDescription: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for creating and managing new Topstitch styles within the Object Browser, ensuring efficient organization and easy access to various Topstitch options for pattern design.

Title: Apply Topstitch Style
Content: Objective Apply Topstitch styles to selected Topstitch(es). Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Operation Select and Apply Another Topstitch Style Select Topstitch(es). Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Assign The style is now being applied to the selected Topstitch. Select and Apply a New Topstitch Style Select Topstitch(es). Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Assign to New Fabric Topstitch Pop-up Menu (Right-click) Assign to New Topstitch A new Topstitch style is now being added to the Topstitch tab and applied to the selected Topstitch at the same time. .
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying and assigning new Topstitch styles to selected Topstitches using the Object Browser Topstitch Tab.

Title: Copy Topstitch Style
Content: Objective Copy and modify an existing Topstitch style in order to change its properties. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Copy Operation Object Browser Select a Topstitch style to copy Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Copy A new Topstitch style with the same properties of the selected Topstitch style is now being copied.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides instructions for copying and modifying an existing Topstitch style to customize its properties using the Object Browser's Topstitch Tab.

Title: Delete Topstitch Style
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Topstitch styles. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch Style Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch Style Delete The selected Topstitch style is now being deleted. Note: It is also possible to delete by pressing the Delete key on the keyboard. A Topstitch style can only be deleted when it is not applied on a Topstitch by clicking the Delete button.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidelines for deleting unnecessary Topstitch styles from the Object Browser's Topstitch Tab, ensuring efficient management of design elements.

Title: Topstitch List Window
Content: Objective It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Topstitch list window. Without any extra setting, Default_Topstitch is applied as default. Once the Default_Topstitch style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it cannot be deleted.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide guidance on how to create, copy, and modify styles within the Topstitch list window, emphasizing the persistence of the Default_Topstitch style until the program is rerun.

Title: Open/ Save Topstitch Style
Content: Objective Open or save preset or custom Topstitch to easily use it in other Project or Garment files. Location Open Object Browser Topstitch Tab Select Desired Topstitch Style Property Editor Open Save Object Browser Topstitch Tab Select Desired Topstitch Style Property Editor Save Operation Open Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Select Desired Topstitch Style Property Editor Open The File Browser window appears. Select the desired Topstitch file and click Open. The selected Topstitch file opens and all properties are reflected in the Property Editor. Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Select Desired Topstitch Style Property Editor Save The File Save window appears. Designate the file saving path and assign Topstitch name. Then, select Save. The Topstitch is saved as a *.sst file and all properties are saved.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for opening and saving preset or custom Topstitch styles to streamline their use in various Project or Garment files.

Title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Topstitch Length
Content: Objective Adjust the stitch length shown on the 3D Pattern. Location Topstitch Item Property Editor Length Operation Find and click the menu indicated in Location The length of the Topstitch will be adjusted according to the set values
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to adjusting the stitch length of a topstitch in the 3D Pattern using the Item Property Editor.

Title: Styleline Editing
Content: Objective Quickly shape patterns in the 3D Window, without the need for previous experience in pattern making. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Styleline Tools 3D Window Edit Styleline Tool Dropdown Menu Operation Load a garment into a scene with an Avatar. Navigate the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". Select a Styleline Editing Tool: Edit Styleline Select an edit point or place on a curve to skew the pattern shape dynamically. Scale Styleline Select a pattern edge and scale it as a whole. Move Styleline Select a pattern edge and move it as singular unit which does not skew. Draw Styleline Draw a new Styleline onto a pattern in the 3D Window. Click on an edge or corner of a pattern piece to begin drawing a new Styleline across it. Click on in the center of the pattern piece to shape the Styleline. Click on another edge or corner of the pattern piece to complete the new Styleline. Manipulate the new Styleline with any of the other Styleline tools. Alter the garment accordingly and watch the patterns update immediately in both the 3D Window and 2D Pattern Window.
ContentDescription: Easily create and manipulate 3D garment patterns in real-time with our intuitive Styleline tools, designed for users of all experience levels.

Title: Line (3D Pattern)
Content: Objective Draw lines directly on 3D Garments (ver3.0.0). Location 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / Line (3D Pattern) (ver5.0.0) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / v (ver5.0.0) Click a point at the desired location of 3D Garments and drag to draw desired 3D lines. Black lines appear and a dot follows around the mouse. Create desired lines or shapes. The created lines or shapes are now highlighted in yellow. The created lines or shapes not only appear as Baselines in 3D Garments but also in 2D Patterns. Note: To complete line creation, double-click on the endpoint. To complete shape creation, the endpoint should be the same as a start point. To create a curved line, press the Ctrl button on the keyboard while creating the line.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for using the 3D Pen tool to draw and create lines or shapes on 3D garments, enhancing the design process with visual feedback and integration into 2D patterns.

Title: Edit Line (3D Pattern)
Content: Objective Edit lines created on 3D Garments. Location 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) (ver.3.0.0)/ Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver.5.0.0) Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) (ver.3.0.0)/ Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver.5.0.0) Click the desired segment. The selected segment is highlighted in yellow To edit, click and drag either end point of the segment to the desired place. The selected point is moved. Delete Right click on the point or segment to be deleted and select the Delete option, or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected point or line is deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing lines on 3D garments using the 3D Toolbar, enabling users to easily select, move, and delete segments within their 3D designs.

Title: Add Point or Curve Point to Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Use the right-click pop-up menu to add a point or curve point to modify Lines (Avatar). Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) When the Avatar is draped in a Garment, the Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the Line (Avatar) where a point or curve point should be added. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Choose Add Point or Add Curve Point as needed. Add Point: a segment point is added to the selected line. Add Curve Point: a curve point is added to the selected line. Select and move the added point or curve point by using the Edit Line (Avatar) tool to edit Line (Avatar).
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the right-click pop-up menu to add and modify points on lines for 3D Avatar garments.

Title: Flatten
Content: Objective Extract Patterns based on lines and shapes created on an Avatar. Note: The Flattening function only extracts closed shapes as Patterns. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Flatten 3D Toolbar Flatten Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Flatten 3D Toolbar Flatten Points no longer appear and only lines appear on the Avatar. Hover the mouse over the shape to be extracted as a Pattern. The area to be flattened appears in light blue. Select all areas to be extracted by holding Shift on the keyboard, then clicking on the desired areas. The selected areas are highlighted in yellow. Hit Enter on the keyboard. The selected areas on the Avatar are converted to patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. The default Fabric is applied to all Patterns created with the Flatten tool. Sewing lines are automatically established for adjacent Patterns. The lines remain on the Avatar.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Flatten tool to extract closed shapes from an Avatar as patterns for 3D garment design.

Title: Flattening as Straight Line
Content: Objective Maintain a particular Line (Avatar) straight when flattening a Pattern. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) When the Avatar is draped, its Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the Line (Avatar) to be flattened as a center front/back or a straight line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Flattening as a Straight Line. The selected line is bolded. The selected line flattens straight.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions on how to maintain a straight line while flattening a garment pattern using the Avatar feature in a 3D editing tool.

Title: Show Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Show or hide lines and shapes created on an Avatar as needed. Location 3D Window Avatar Display Show Lines (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Avatar Display Show Lines (Avatar) All lines and shapes on the Avatar appear or hide. Note: When the Avatar is hidden, the lines and shapes are hidden as well.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to toggle the visibility of lines and shapes on an Avatar within a 3D display environment.

Title: Edit Line (3D Pattern) Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Edit desired 3D Pen lines using the right-click pop-up menu. Location 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver5.0.0) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) (ver3.0.0). / Edit Line (3D Pattern) (ver5.0.0) Right click on the desired 3D Pen line. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Refer to the below table and select an appropriate option. Option Description Delete Delete the selected 3D Pen line. Add Point Add a Segment Point to the selected 3D Pen line. Add Curve Point Add a Curve Point to the selected 3D Pen line. Cut Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Cut &amp Sew Cut and sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Symmetric Cut Cut the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Cut &amp Sew Cut and sew the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. Trace as Internal Shape Trace the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern. Convert to Internal Shape Convert the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on how to edit 3D Pen lines using the right-click pop-up menu in the 3D Toolbar for garment design and pattern editing.

Title: Edit Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Edit lines created on an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Click on the line or the shape to be selected. The line or the shape is selected and highlighted in yellow. While the line of the shape is selected, click and drag to move the selected item to the desired position. Delete Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Select the line or the shape to be deleted. Right click on the selected item and select Delete or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected line or shape is deleted. Note: To select multiple lines or shapes, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard, then click on additional lines or shapes. To select all lines and shapes on the Avatar, hit the Ctrl+A on the keyboard. After the lines and shapes are drawn on the Avatar, if you delete the Avatar, all previously created lines, and shapes are also deleted.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing, moving, and deleting lines and shapes on an Avatar within a 3D garment design interface.

Title: Create Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Draw lines on an Avatar and extract Patterns. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Line (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Line (Avatar) If there is a Garment on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Hover the mouse over the Avatar. A black dot follows the mouse. Click on the desired position on the Avatar to create lines or shapes. The lines or shapes appear on the Avatar in black. Click on the start point to complete drawing the line. The lines or shapes are created on the Avatar. Note: To create a curve point while drawing lines on the Avatar, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click on the Avatar. Hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action or hit the Esc key or Ctrl+Z to cancel all actions. All lines and shapes drawn on the Avatar are saved when you save the file in Project, Garment, or Avatar file format.
ContentDescription: This web page enables users to draw lines and shapes on a translucent Avatar to extract and save intricate patterns for garment design.

Title: Tack
Content: Objective Use this function to visualize fit adjustments by tacking temporarily. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack 3D Toolbar Tack Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack 3D Toolbar Tack Click on an initial point on a draped Garment. A point is now being created with a dotted line following. Click on an endpoint. Another point is now being created with a yellow highlighted line. Same tack is now being created in the 2D Pattern. Activate Simulate. The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to each other. Note: It is also available to create and modify tacks in the 2D window (ver3.1.0).
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for visualizing fit adjustments in garment design through the temporary tacking function in both 3D and 2D environments.

Title: Tack on Avatar
Content: Objective Temporarily fix a point of a Garment to an Avatar. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Click on a point of a 3D Garment to fix. A point is now being created and a dotted line follows along the mouse cursor, and the selected garment becomes semi-transparent. Click on a point of an Avatar. The selected Garment is now being opaque once again. Same tack is now being created in the corresponding 2D Pattern. Activate Simulate. The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to the Avatar.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for temporarily tacking a garment to an avatar in a 3D environment, allowing users to achieve precise garment simulation.
